notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 2 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "Sample Statement of Assurance" is an h6 with no h5 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Turn a heading that is only a link into a button
decisions.why: "Sample Statement of Assurance" is written as a section heading but its whole content is a link, so the contents list offers to jump to a section that is really a document.

decisions.label: Move the document button into the banner
decisions.why: "Sample Statement of Assurance" is the only action on the page and it was written as a heading. In the banner it is the first thing a reader sees rather than something they scroll to.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 1 link on this page opens a file — 1 PDF — and says nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Remove the in-page copy of a banner button
decisions.why: "Sample Statement of Assurance" is now a button in the banner, so this second copy further down the page says the same thing again.
